title: Emergency bucket toilet
summary: Line a toilet bowl or 5-gallon bucket with two bags, add an absorbent, tie off, store, and wash your hands.

sources.title: NC DHHS: Toilet Use During an Emergency
King County Public Health (WA): Emergency toilets

blocks.text: If the toilet won't flush, the water is off, or the sewer isn't working, use a bag-lined toilet or bucket. **Option 1:** use a working toilet at a neighbor's, friend's, or business.

blocks.alt: Bucket toilet. A 5-gallon pail with a toilet seat and a closed lid, lined with two heavy-duty bags, one inside the other, with absorbent such as cat litter, sawdust, ashes, peat moss or lime at the bottom. Keep it away from where you prepare or eat food, and at least 100 feet from lakes, rivers, streams and wells. After each use: add more absorbent if needed, tie the bag shut tightly when it is part full, move it at the end of the day to a protected place such as a garage, basement or outbuilding inside a trash can away from kids and animals, put in a fresh double bag, and wash your hands with soap and water. Do not dump waste in the yard, a creek or a storm drain. Disposal is a working sewer or septic system, or burying it on your own property.
blocks.caption: A bag-lined bucket toilet and what to do after each use.

items: Pick a spot **away from where you prepare or eat food**. Keep it at least **100 feet** from lakes, rivers, streams and wells if you can.
Toilet bowl method: turn off the water valve and flush out the water still in the bowl so it doesn't refill. Or use a **5-gallon pail** with a toilet seat if you have one.
Line the bowl or bucket with **two heavy-duty garbage bags** (one inside the other).
Add an **absorbent** to the bottom: cat litter, sawdust, fireplace ashes, peat moss or lime. It soaks up liquid and cuts odor.
Keep lids and covers closed. Supervise small children.
When the bag is part full, **tie it shut tightly**. At the end of each day, move it to a protected place (garage, basement or outbuilding), inside a trash can, away from kids and animals.
Put in a fresh double bag.
**Wash your hands** with soap and water. No running water? Use wet wipes and sanitizer.

blocks.text: **Don't dump waste in the yard, a creek or a storm drain.** Disposal: a working public sewer or septic system, or burying it on your own property. During a declared emergency, King County says bagged waste may go in regular trash **only if an official announcement allows it**. Check with Henrico Emergency Management at (804) 501-5162 before you put any bag at the curb.
Disinfect a reusable bucket with bleach or throw it away. For bleach amounts on surfaces, see the hygiene guide.
Stock now: heavy-duty garbage bags (two per use), cat litter or sawdust, a 5-gallon bucket, soap and wipes. Dug latrines aren't appropriate in urban areas.
